newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina attacks Brazil car industry policy.
newsitem.headline: Argentina attacks Brazil car industry policy.

text.p: The Argentine government Tuesday accused Brazil of producing regulations "tailor made" to attract investments to its country's car industry in prejudice of its partners in the Mercosur customs union.
Brazil last week launched a program of subsidies to attract investments in the north, northeast and west of Brazil including tariff cuts of up to 35 percent for importing car parts.
Immediately after the Brazilian move, South Korea's Asia Motors Co Ltd announced it was investing $500 million in a factory to build passenger vehicles in Brazil.
"I think this was a tailor-made measure, because this company (Asia Motors) reacted very quickly," Argentina's International Economic Relations Secretary Jorge Campbell told reporters.
He added that the Brazilian move had sparked "concern" within the Argentine government and that Argentina was studying whether it breached any Mercosur agreement.
"We are going to be clear and firm and we will make our demands if any Mercosur accord is being violated," Campbell said.
The Mercosur customs union groups Argentina and Brazil with Uruguay and Paraguay. Chile and Bolivia recently agreed free trade pacts with the bloc.
